cohort.transition_reason: Joint City Council & Board of County Commissioners sessions held in 2017.

cohesion.label: High Consensus

overall_blocs.summary: No recorded split votes in this scope yet (board voted unanimously on tracked motions).

conflicts.issue: Scope and Viability of Proposed Joint Youth Engagement Coordinator
conflicts.summary: Committee members disagreed on whether a single jointly funded youth coordinator could avoid the failure of the 1990s Youth Coordinating Board, whether to focus on internal coordination versus a public-facing 'youth center without walls' and web portal, and whether to restrict the initial target age group to 4–14 rather than 5–24.
conflicts.side_a_position: Limit initial scope (such as ages 4–14), focus on public-facing engagement tools rather than internal bureaucracy, and guard against repeat coordination failures or staff creep.
side_a_arguments: The 1990s Youth Coordinating Board had a director and roughly three staff members and still collapsed.
Coordinating dozens of countywide youth providers risks 'herding cats' and generating requests for three or four additional support staff.
Residents and youth urgently need a single website, social media hub, and 'youth center without walls' rather than internal agency coordination.
Narrowing initial scope to ages 4–14 or 5–14 would make the workload more manageable before expanding.
conflicts.side_b_position: Proceed with the budgeted 50-50 position covering ages 5–24 by focusing internally on City and County programs first and refining scope as implementation moves forward.
side_b_arguments: Staff designed the initial scope around internal City and County programs specifically to avoid overreaching like past initiatives.
While ages 5–14 primarily involve DPS and Parks & Recreation, most major youth financial resources and programs serve ages 14–24.
With funding included in both draft budgets, the boards should move forward rather than backward and adjust course after June work sessions.
conflicts.resolution: No committee vote was taken; the proposal was slated to go before the full City Council and Board of County Commissioners at their June work sessions for review and vote.

conflicts.issue: Geographic Equity, Structure, and Cost-Sharing of the Housing Stabilization Grant/Forgivable Loan Pilot
conflicts.summary: Staff and committee members debated whether a proposed $222,000 Reinvestment Partners pilot targeting Southside homeowners with 60%+ property appreciation was legally, administratively, and geographically equitable compared to countywide tax-relief outreach and home-repair assistance.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support targeted housing stabilization (particularly forgivable loans in Southside) to protect vulnerable long-term homeowners from displacement caused by rapid assessment spikes.
side_a_arguments: Targets the most vulnerable homeowners experiencing extraordinary (60%+) property appreciation relative to the 12% average.
Revitalizing neighborhoods like Southside generates far more in long-term property tax revenue than the $222,000–$272,000 program cost.
Can be paired with broader outreach on existing tax-relief programs and a housing repair co-op so homeowners can afford repairs and taxes.
conflicts.side_b_position: Question neighborhood-specific subsidies and Reinvestment Partners pilot mechanics due to taxpayer equity complaints, overlapping relief programs, legal contracting limits, and data inconsistencies.
side_b_arguments: Tax and call-center staff are already fielding complaints from residents elsewhere in Durham asking why one neighborhood receives aid while other homeowners with rising taxes do not.
Some targeted Southside parcels already receive elderly or disabled tax offsets, and five properties with 32% increases elsewhere were excluded.

The proposal contained conflicting household figures (524, 217, and 324), potential legal barriers to contracting with Reinvestment Partners, and a heavily County-weighted split ($151,000 County vs. $71,400 City).
conflicts.resolution: A motion referenced to Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow was seconded to bring the proposal back in March after individual boards and staff review it further, including implications of shifting to three-year and four-year property revaluations (the final vote call fell in an omitted digest gap).

meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee
meetings.executive_summary: The Joint City-County Committee, presided over by BOCC Chair Wendy Jacobs (with Mayor Bill Bell joining during the session), unanimously approved the August 8, 2017 minutes and advanced planning for a proposed City-County fire department consolidation targeting a July 1, 2018 launch. Following a presentation by City Fire Chief Dan Curia, County Fire Rescue Chief Reggie Velines, and Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson, the committee passed a unanimous voice vote directing staff to continue planning the merger and return in the spring with final interlocal documents for both governing boards. Members also began discussing the joint City-County appointment to the GoTriangle Board of Trustees and passed two unanimous voice votes on a clean energy/climate resolution: directing staff and the Environmental Affairs Board (EAB) to incorporate Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow's revisions by December, and directing the managers to report back in February on updates to the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reduction Plan. Finally, the committee directed staff to explore joint City-County budget outreach sessions and recognized retiring members, honoring Mayor Bill Bell for over four decades of local public service.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Approval of August 8, 2017 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: BOCC Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order with a quorum present and noted she would wait for Mayor Bill Bell's arrival before considering moving up the GoTriangle appointment item. The committee then reviewed the minutes from the August 8, 2017 meeting with no corrections offered.

agenda_items.title: City-County Fire Department Consolidation Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Fire Chief Dan Curia, County Fire Rescue Chief Reggie Velines, and Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson presented a feasibility white paper to merge City and County fire operations in eastern and southern Durham (including the former Bethesda and Parkwood service district) by July 1, 2018. Staff explained that intermingled response boundaries currently force units to cross jurisdictions and outlined a permanent interlocal financial framework, pay-plan alignment, co-located EMS, and eventual closure of Old Page Road and Parkwood stations once new City stations open. Committee members praised the collaborative staff work, noted potential ISO rating improvements and public outreach needs, and clarified that advancing the planning work leaves final approval of interlocal agreements to the full City Council and Board of County Commissioners in the spring.

agenda_items.title: City-County Appointment to GoTriangle Board of Trustees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Wendy Jacobs asked Mayor Bill Bell to move up Item 5 regarding the joint City-County appointment to the GoTriangle Board of Trustees. Members reviewed the history of the joint seat alongside the City and County individual seats, noted that an incumbent planned to cycle off due to a church schedule conflict, and discussed checking clerk records on past appointment procedures. (The remainder of this item occurred during a truncated portion of the transcript digest.)
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote recorded in transcript

agenda_items.title: Clean Energy Resolution and Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reduction Plan Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming mid-discussion on an aspirational clean energy policy resolution and Durham's 12-year-old Greenhouse Gas Action Plan, members debated whether to seek Environmental Affairs Board (EAB) and Sustainability Office input by December or February. To give staff adequate review time without delaying the resolution, the committee adopted a two-stage approach: asking managers and staff to work with the EAB on Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow's added 'whereas' clauses for a December return, and separately directing managers to report in February on short- and long-term updates to the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reduction Plan.

agenda_items.title: Joint City-County Budget Outreach (Coffees with Council Collaboration)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members discussed holding joint City-County budget outreach meetings alongside the City's PAC-hosted 'Coffees with Council' so residents gain a unified view of how both local governments spend tax dollars. Council Member Jillian Johnson and other members highlighted challenges with low attendance at standalone library sessions and suggested co-locating with existing community meetings. The committee informally directed City and County manager and clerk staff to confer and return with recommendations ahead of the budget cycle.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Outgoing Members and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the close of the meeting, members acknowledged two colleagues who would not return to the committee and paid special tribute to Mayor Bill Bell for roughly 40 years of public service—including 26 years as a County Commissioner, leadership in the school system merger, and decades of City-County collaboration—before adjourning.

votes.notes: Voice vote; individual attendees and mover/seconder were not identified by name in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: No corrections were requested prior to the motion and second.

votes.item_title: Continue Planning for City-County Fire Department Consolidation
votes.notes: Voice vote; mover, seconder, and individual voter names were not identified in the transcript (Commissioner Heidi Carter was noted in the audience).
votes.discussion_detail: Motion adopted staff recommendations as amended in bullet 6 to direct staff to continue planning to merge the two fire departments and bring final interlocal agreements back to the City Council and BOCC in the spring.

votes.item_title: EAB and Staff Review of Clean Energy Resolution for December Return
votes.notes: Voice vote; mover, seconder, and individual voter names were not identified in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Directed managers and staff to work with the Environmental Affairs Board (EAB) to incorporate Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow's draft additions and return to the committee in December on the resolution itself.

votes.item_title: Managers' Report on Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reduction Plan for February Return
votes.notes: Voice vote; mover, seconder, and individual voter names were not identified in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Directed the City and County managers to revisit the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reduction Plan and report back in February on progress, short-term actions, and long-term revisions in light of the resolution.

meetings.title: Joint City/County Committee
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Joint City/County Committee unanimously approved the March 14, 2017 minutes by voice vote and heard informational briefings on Lake Michie park fees, youth violence prevention, joint youth coordination, and County tax call center operations. Resident Richard Miller challenged Durham Parks and Recreation's two-tier Lake Michie fee surcharge for non-city residents, prompting the committee to refer his detailed data to the City and County Managers for review. Dr. Wanda Boone of Together for Resilient Youth (TRY) outlined a public-health violence prevention initiative centered on Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) and requested meeting space plus $150,000 in seed funding for youth peer-educator stipends. Management Analyst Maddie Sistivas presented a 50-50 jointly funded youth engagement coordinator proposal ahead of June governing-board work sessions, sparking debate over past coordination failures, internal versus external focus, and target age ranges before the committee agreed to reconvene on August 8, 2017.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Approval of March 14, 2017 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 9:04 a.m. with a quorum present. With no adjustments to the agenda, the committee moved and seconded approval of the March 14, 2017 minutes.

agenda_items.title: Lake Michie Recreational Usage Two-Tier Fee Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Richard Miller (listed as Ryan Miller) presented an analysis showing that Durham Parks and Recreation's $5 and $15 surcharges on non-city residents at Lake Michie result in fees 145% to over 200% higher for county residents outside city limits. Committee members asked whether the surcharge applies across all parks facilities and compared it to double water rates outside city limits, then asked Miller to submit his detailed figures to the City and County Managers for review.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Youth Violence Prevention Presentation (Together for Resilient Youth)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Wanda Boone presented a public-health youth violence prevention framework built on Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs), resilience training, and existing coalitions including College TRY, the Good Neighbor Business Initiative, faith partners, and Project BUILD. She requested additional meeting space and $150,000 in seed funding to support stipends and incentives for roughly 50 youth peer educators in Northeast Central Durham and District 4. Members discussed linking Dr. Boone with the County's Healthy 2020 resolution, training Bull City United outreach workers in ACEs and resilience, and reviewing the $150,000 budget.

agenda_items.title: Joint Youth Engagement Coordinator Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Management Analyst Maddie Sistivas outlined a proposal for a 50-50 jointly funded City-County youth engagement coordinator position, incorporating Youth Commission feedback and scheduled for review at June City Council and BOCC work sessions. Several members voiced skepticism citing the collapse of Durham's 1990s Youth Coordinating Board, questioned potential staff expansion, and urged prioritizing a public-facing portal or 'youth center without walls' rather than internal coordination. Council Member Don Moffitt suggested starting with ages 4 to 14, whereas another member noted major resources sit in the 14-to-24 range and urged keeping the funding in both draft budgets while refining scope.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Tax Call Center and Durham One Call Coordination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming mid-discussion, staff explained why the Durham County Tax Office call center (560-0300) should remain separate from Durham One Call rather than routing citizens through multi-step transfers, noting callers can press zero to reach a representative directly for complex tax inquiries. Members remarked that the County's general 560-0300 line functions as 'the best kept secret' and suggested better publicizing the number.

agenda_items.title: Next Meeting Scheduling (August 8, 2017) and Upcoming Studies
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members agreed to schedule the next Joint City-County Committee meeting for August 8, 2017, at the Durham County Commissioners so staff can present the TJCOG livability index tool for the age-friendly community initiative. A member also recommended inviting Duke Sanford School graduate students to present a workforce study showing that while Durham County has the highest wages in North Carolina, only 30% of county residents hold jobs in the county and resident employment in RTP declined from 19% in 2002 to 15% in 2014.

votes.notes: Voice vote declared unanimous by Chair Bill Bell; mover, seconder, and individual attendees were not named in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion and second to approve the March 14, 2017 minutes passed with no opposition.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Joint City-County Committee unanimously approved the November 29, 2016 minutes by voice vote and received a major GoTriangle financial update on the Durham-Orange Light Rail Project. Project Director Danny Rogers reported that financial restructuring closed the funding gap identified in December 2016 without requiring new local funds in the base case, presenting a $2.476 billion year-of-expenditure budget through a 2028 opening that incorporates an NCCU station and $35 million in university and local right-of-way commitments. Committee members also challenged a local museum expansion team to pursue a one-third private fundraising match (~$750,000) alongside City and County capital support. Extensive debate centered on a proposed $222,000 Housing Stabilization Grant and Forgivable Loan pilot with Reinvestment Partners, where staff and members raised geographic equity, administrative, and data-consistency concerns before a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow was seconded to revisit the proposal in March.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Approval of November 29, 2016 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order with four members present, constituting a quorum. With no corrections or agenda adjustments, the committee approved the November 29, 2016 minutes by unanimous voice vote.

agenda_items.title: GoTriangle Update: Durham-Orange Light Rail Project Financial Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: GoTriangle Project Director Danny Rogers reported that updated cash-flow financing closed the funding gap identified in December 2016 without additional local funds in the base case, yielding a $2.476 billion FTA budget ($1.877 billion in 2016 dollars) with an extended 2028 opening, a North Carolina Central University station, Hillsborough station adjustments, and ~$35 million in committed public and university right-of-way donations. Rogers outlined tight engineering and funding milestones from April 2017 design contracts through a June 2018 65%-design submission for the President's budget and a 2019–2020 Full Funding Grant Agreement. Members praised linking NCCU with Duke and UNC, Council Member Eddie Davis asked about the new federal administration, Don Moffitt had raised commuter rail questions, and a BOCC member urged City partnership on revenue due diligence such as tax increment financing.

agenda_items.title: Museum Expansion Public-Private Capital Funding Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming mid-discussion with museum representatives (Katie and Ruth), members voiced support for the project while noting heavy City-County capital demands for light rail and Pre-K. One member challenged the museum's board to structure construction financing as a one-third/one-third/one-third public-private partnership by raising approximately $750,000 privately, citing past million-dollar private campaigns for the Senior Center and Durham Literacy Center.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Housing Stabilization Grants and Forgivable Loans (Reinvestment Partners)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The committee reviewed a $222,000 City-County pilot ($151,000 County share and $71,400 City share, including $60,000 in administration) to contract with Reinvestment Partners for housing stabilization grants and forgivable loans to low-income homeowners experiencing steep post-revaluation property appreciation (60%+ vs. 12% average). Tax and call-center staff warned that some Southside properties already receive elderly/disabled tax offsets and that residents across Durham are questioning why relief would target one neighborhood, while members also flagged conflicting household counts (524, 217, and 324), legal contracting hurdles, and the County's higher cost share. Supporters countered that Southside revitalization yields net property tax gains and urged pairing outreach with existing tax relief and home repair co-op programs; Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow's motion to revisit the proposal in March was seconded before a gap in the digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Motion to revisit in March moved and seconded (vote outcome omitted in digest gap)

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Joint Session Scheduling and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members briefly confirmed a joint Pre-K meeting on their calendars for April 27 at 1:30 p.m. Mayor Bill Bell adjourned the meeting at 11:26 a.m.

votes.notes: Voice vote declared unanimous by Chair Bill Bell with a four-member quorum noted at opening; mover, seconder, and individual voter names were not recorded in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion and second to approve the November 29, 2016 minutes passed with no corrections or opposition.
